chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqi from Abu al-Bakhtari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'For every divorced woman there is a mut'ah (congratulatory gift), except for the mu'talah (woman who buys her own freedom from divorce), for she has purchased herself.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali)
key_terms.الْمُخْتَلِعَة: Al-Mu'talah (a woman who initiates divorce by paying compensation to the husband)
key_terms.مُتْعَة: Mut'ah (congratulatory gift given to the wife upon divorce)

ai.seo_question: Who is exempt from receiving the mut'ah gift upon divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between standard divorce and 'khul'' (redemption), where the wife buys her freedom. It establishes that since the 'mu'talah' has already compensated the husband for her release, she is not entitled to the additional voluntary gift of 'mut'ah', a ruling deeply rooted in the principles of equity within Shia fiqh. The chain of transmission highlights the continuity of this legal understanding from Imam Ali (AS) through the early scholars like al-Barqi.
